title: Saimemory Moves To Commercialize Z-Angle Memory (ZAM)
key_facts: Saimemory, a Tokyo-based subsidiary of Japan's SoftBank formed in 2024, has signed a memorandum of understanding with Shinko Electric.
The two companies will develop and commercialise Saimemory's Z-Angle Memory (ZAM), which is still in R&D and is designed for high bandwidth in AI applications.
Shinko is a Nagano-based supplier of substrates for packaging and leadframes; through the partnership it plans to establish the packaging and manufacturing technologies needed for ZAM.
Earlier this year Saimemory signed an agreement with Intel to commercialise ZAM.
ZAM appears to be an alternative to HBM, which is in short supply and expensive.
Saimemory's president and CEO, Hideya Yamaguchi, said the agreement will accelerate practical implementation of ZAM.
